an3.84:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Vesālī in the Great Forest.
an3.84:1.2: Then a certain Vajjian monk approached him and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One,
an3.84:1.3: “Lord, this recitation of more than 150 training rules comes every fortnight.
an3.84:1.4: I cannot train in reference to them.”
an3.84:1.5: “Monk, can you train in reference to the three trainings:
an3.84:1.6: the training in heightened virtue, the training in heightened mind, the training in heightened discernment?”
an3.84:1.7: “Yes, lord, I can train in reference to the three trainings:
an3.84:1.8: the training in heightened virtue, the training in heightened mind, the training in heightened discernment.”
an3.84:1.9: “Then train in reference to those three trainings:
an3.84:1.10: the training in heightened virtue, the training in heightened mind, the training in heightened discernment.
an3.84:2.1: As you train in heightened virtue, heightened mind, & heightened discernment, your passion, aversion, & delusion—when trained in heightened virtue, heightened mind, & heightened discernment—will be abandoned.
an3.84:2.2: You—with the abandoning of passion, the abandoning of aversion, the abandoning of delusion—will not do anything unskillful or engage in any evil.”
an3.84:3.1: Later on, that monk trained in reference to heightened virtue, heightened mind, & heightened discernment.
an3.84:3.2: His passion, aversion, & delusion—when trained in heightened virtue, heightened mind, & heightened discernment were abandoned.
an3.84:3.3: He—with the abandoning of passion, the abandoning of aversion, the abandoning of delusion—did not do anything unskillful or engage in any evil.
